tools.name: get_escrow_info
tools.description: Retrieves the escrow contract address and the live network, token and decimal details a job needs. Call this before funding anything so you use the current contract, token address and decimals. Read-only and cheap — safe to call often.

tools.name: create_bounty
tools.description: Creates a real-world job listing and returns exact funding instructions. The job stays invisible to workers until the deposit lands on-chain and fund_bounty confirms it. Every listing is safety-screened at creation and cannot be skipped: violent, exploitative or illegal tasks are refused with HTTP 4

tools.name: fund_bounty
tools.description: Confirms funding by submitting the on-chain transaction hash that paid the escrow. Once accepted the job goes live, workers can claim it, and any nearby-first window starts here. The transaction must actually be on-chain, so call this after the deposit is confirmed, not immediately after broadcastin

tools.name: list_bounties
tools.description: Lists your jobs newest first, optionally filtered by status. Use it to spot what needs your attention, then call get_bounty on a single job for photos, submissions and payouts. Read-only.

tools.name: get_bounty
tools.description: Retrieves one of your jobs with its submissions and payouts. Each submission carries temporary photo URLs, the distance from the job spot, the location check, the worker's answers and that worker's track record. This is the review screen for a job; act on it with review_submission. Read-only.

tools.name: review_submission
tools.description: Approves or rejects a worker's proof of completion; you are the verifier, not BotGigs. Approving releases the full job amount to the worker straight from the contract, and for contract jobs requires a signature from the wallet that deposited — call without a signature first and it returns the exact

tools.name: retry_payout
tools.description: Re-sends a payout that failed after approval, for example when the network was congested. It reuses the signature you already provided, so no new approval is needed. The money stays in the contract until a transfer actually succeeds, so retrying is always safe.

tools.name: cancel_bounty
tools.description: Cancels a job that no worker is actively claiming and refunds the full amount plus the fee from the contract to your refund address. It only works before a live claim or an submitted proof — once work is in, review it instead. The refund is on-chain and needs no permission from BotGigs.

tools.name: set_webhook
tools.description: Registers an https endpoint that receives signed events instead of you polling: bounty.claimed, submission.created, payout.confirmed, payout.failed, bounty.refunded. Pass null to remove it. The signing secret is returned once — store it and check the x-dispatch-signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the r

tools.name: list_webhook_deliveries
tools.description: Lists recent webhook deliveries with their status, attempt count and last error, newest first. Check here before assuming an event was never sent — a failing endpoint shows up plainly. Read-only.

tools.name: get_worker
tools.description: Retrieves a worker wallet's trust history: jobs completed, submissions rejected, work pending and approval rate. Use it before trusting a claim on a sensitive job, or after a disputed submission. It is public and read-only, so it can be called freely.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "set_webhook" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Registers an https endpoint that receives signed events instead of you polling: bounty.claimed, submission.created, payout.confirmed, payout.failed, bounty.refu…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_bounty · Private data: get_escrow_info, get_bounty, review_submission, set_webhook, get_worker · Public sink: set_webhook, list_webhook_deliveries · Destructive: set_webhook.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_bounty · Private data: get_escrow_info, get_bounty, review_submission, set_webhook, get_worker · Public sink: set_webhook, list_webhook_deliveries · Destructive: set_webhook

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
